name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Thermal Lance TL-9 'Sunstroke'
description: A shoulder-mounted directed thermal weapon that projects a focused infrared beam capable of raising surface temperatures to 1,800°C within a two-second exposure window. The TL-9 was designed for breaching reinforced structures and disabling armored vehicles, but its effectiveness against personnel has made it a feared anti-infantry weapon in corporate conflict zones. The beam is invisible to the naked eye — targets only know they have been hit when their equipment begins to glow.
legality: Military restricted — active deployment authorization required
specifications:
beam wavelength: 1064nm focused infrared
power output: 45kW sustained
effective range: 15-120 meters
beam duration: 2-second pulse, 4-second recharge
weight: 8.2 kg with power pack
power source: Dedicated dorsal capacitor pack, 12 pulses per charge
story_hooks: A stolen TL-9 has been used to cut through the vault wall of a Tier 3 credit union — the theft was surgical, the beam pattern suggests military training.
Arcturus is recalling TL-9 units after discovering the capacitor pack can be overcharged to produce a single catastrophic pulse — essentially turning it into a one-shot building-killer.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist shoulder-mounted cannon with a pronounced forward-raking stance. The barrel assembly dominates the profile — a chunky, heat-sink-ribbed cylinder that tapers slightly toward the muzzle. The weapon has an aggressive, purposeful geometry that reads as purely military. The capacitor pack forms a heavy dorsal hump behind the breech, creating a distinctive silhouette when shouldered.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 94 cm | Barrel length: 52 cm | Width at capacitor pack: 18 cm | Height from mounting rail to top of heat dissipation fins: 24 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and front-heavy — the barrel assembly pulls the center of mass forward, requiring braced shouldering. The 8.2 kg distributed load feels substantial but manageable for a two-handed mount. Users describe it as 'anchor-like but purposeful.'
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade titanium alloy frame with tungsten thermal-sink barrel assembly. Capacitor pack housing is reinforced carbon composite with embedded copper heat-dissipation pathways visible through semi-translucent resin sections.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal black with raw brushed-metal heat dissipation fins running the length of the barrel. The titanium frame shows deliberate tool marks and micro-scratches from field handling. Capacitor housing has a satin finish with visible thermal scorch marks from repeated charge cycles.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal black primary with brushed silver-gray barrel ribbing. Accent colors: deep orange around the muzzle aperture (heat-resistant optical coating), thin crimson warning striping along the capacitor pack.
physical_description.grip_texture: The rear grip assembly is wrapped in reinforced non-slip rubber with a slight chevron pattern. The foregrip (mounted on the barrel assembly for stabilization) features knurled titanium beneath a thin grippy polymer overlay. The shoulder cup is padded with ceramic-infused foam designed to dissipate heat transfer.
distinctive_features: Prominent spiral heat-sink fins running the full length of the barrel — actively cool to the touch between cycles but glow faintly orange after sustained fire
Recessed thermal bloom containment optics mounted just forward of the breech — a cluster of small hexagonal apertures that appear to shift color from amber to pale blue depending on charge state
Dual capacitor status LEDs on the dorsal pack: one red (low charge), one amber (partial charge), one green (ready) — cycling in sequence during recharge cycles
Muzzle aperture appears as a flat, slightly recessed circular opening with faint concentric rings — the focusing lens is recessed 3 cm behind the muzzle face
Integrated pressure-relief vents along the sides of the barrel assembly — small slotted openings that hiss quietly during thermal dissipation
Weapon-mounted thermal profiler lens: a small secondary optic mounted at 45-degree angle on the left side of the breech, allowing operator sight-line confirmation of target heating
Scorch marks and micro-fractures around the muzzle and barrel flanges from repeated thermal cycling — evidence of field stress
Mounting rail underside shows a series of alignment marks and calibration scratches
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Arcturus Defense Solutions logo (a stylized compass rose with thermal wave motif) stamped in deep relief on the left side of the capacitor pack. 'SUNSTROKE TL-9' engraved in military stencil font on the right barrel flange. Iron Point Ammunition subsidiary stamp on the dorsal capacitor housing. Serial number laser-etched along the underside of the mounting rail. Faint crossed-circle 'military restricted' warning symbol molded into the grip assembly.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but meticulously maintained. The weapon shows evidence of active deployment: scorch marks, minor dents in the capacitor housing, heat-stress discoloration around the muzzle. However, the heat-sink fins are clean, optics are clear, and all LEDs function crisply. Operators of this tier-4+ weapon treat it with professional care — corrosion is minimal, wear patterns are uniform. The rubber grip shows compression marks from gloved hands.

Camera angle: 3/4 view from the left, weapon mounted on a burnished steel maintenance rack against a deep charcoal matte background. Dramatic side-lighting from a warm orange-tinted key light, casting sharp shadows that emphasize the barrel's heat-sink ribbing and the capacitor pack's dimensional depth.
